fix_commit_message:
avcodec/adpcm: signed integer overflow in ADPCM_N64

Fixes: signed integer overflow

Found-by: Marius Momeu <marius.momeu@berkeley.edu>
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix b45a6d3f76f1 on top of intro 5fc9c79f53d7 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (IntegerOverflow): The ADPCM Silicon Graphics N64 decoder in libavcodec/adpcm.c computes a predictor 'delta' value by summing products of decoded sample codes and 16-bit filter coefficients that are read from (attacker-controlled) codec extradata. The multiplication of these signed int values can overflow the range of 'int', which is undefined behavior in C and was detected by UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer during fuzz testing (OSS-Fuzz). An earlier commit (0c7e0ed35b) had already changed the accumulator 'delta' to unsigned and cast the sum before division, addressing overflow in the addition, but the multiplication 'sf_codes[...] * coefs[...]' itself remained purely signed, so the intermediate product could still overflow before assignment/addition. Commit b45a6d3f76 fixes this remaining case by casting one operand of the multiplication to unsigned. Root cause: The ADPCM_N64 decoder trusts filter coefficient values loaded from codec extradata (attacker-controlled) and multiplies them with decoded sample codes using plain signed 'int' arithmetic without any range validation or use of unsigned/wider arithmetic, allowing the product to exceed INT_MAX/underflow INT_MIN, which is undefined behavior in C.
